name: Model routing
subject: Which model serves a request, by how sensitive its content is and how hard it is. Routing stays inside one family: the clients' credentials are not interchangeable across providers.

no_eligible.note: enforce, when no model in the family is both eligible for the content and allowed for the caller's key: block (reject the request with an error), keep (send it to the requested model; the log marks the violation) or fallback_model (send it to `model`, which the key must be allowed to call; otherwise block). Shadow only logs the action.

require_same_note: LiteLLM applies model-level guardrails (litellm_params.guardrails) and the key's per-model rpm / tpm limits and budget for the requested model before this hook runs, and not again for the model it picks. true: a model whose guardrails (or limits) differ from the requested model's is never chosen; the log lists it under excluded. The requested model itself is always allowed.
paths_to_jev_note: full: every path as written. shape_outside_repo: paths inside the agent's working directory as repo-relative paths, others as their file name plus [outside repo, sensitive] flags. shape: every path as file name plus flags. restricted_paths are always matched on the full path, locally.

fallback.note: Any Jev error or timeout: treat the content as restricted and the task as medium.

sensitivity.restricted_at_note: Treat the request as restricted when P(restricted) + P(proprietary) reaches this, whatever the top choice was.

public.note: Any model in the family; cheapest first.

tiers.note: difficulty is a 0-2 score whose levels are the tiers in order. up_at: the tier is the highest whose probability mass P(level >= tier) reaches its threshold, so a hesitant answer routes up (under-tiering costs quality, over-tiering only money). from_score: used instead when an answer has no probabilities (the fallback) or up_at is absent; the tier is the highest whose threshold the expected score reaches. A model of a higher tier may serve a lower one, never the reverse.

stickiness.note: Mid-conversation, a cheaper model is only taken when (context x cache_read_factor + turn_tokens) x (old - new input price) x remaining_turns exceeds context x new input price, the cost of the new model reprocessing the whole context. remaining_turns 1: the switch must pay for itself on the next turn, because nobody knows how many turns are left; at 1/cache_read_factor turns the context term cancels and every cheaper model wins. Moves to a higher tier, and moves forced by sensitivity, always happen.

claude.note: Claude Code via the forwarded subscription login. A request is routed when its model is one of these (a dated or suffixed id such as claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 counts) or an alias; any other model is left alone. Prices are list USD per million input tokens; edit to your contract. max_context (optional, tokens): the model is skipped when the estimated context is larger.

chatgpt.note: Codex via the ChatGPT subscription. Prices are placeholders for relative cost; edit to your contract.
